Hi Lena — thanks for the clear list. See answers below (short form) and I attached a one-page retention matrix and our SOC 2 summary for quick review. Happy to provide formal DPA/contract language once you confirm you want an EU-hosted tenancy.

Q: EU-only hosted account?
A: Yes — for Enterprise customers we offer region-isolated Hosted API deployments (EU, US, APAC). An EU-hosted account keeps primary storage and processing within EU datacenters and is covered under our EU Data Processing Addendum (DPA). Self-serve accounts default to our global hosted fleet (US by default); please request EU tenancy during onboarding to ensure isolation.

Q: Default retention windows (Hosted API)
- Request/response payloads (full request and model output): retained by default for 30 days for operational debugging and abuse prevention.
- Debug/structured logs (traces, error logs): retained 90 days.
- Aggregated telemetry and billing metrics (token counts, latency histograms): retained 24 months in aggregated form; no customer-identifiable payloads in aggregated metrics.

Q: Deletion process and timelines
- We provide an Admin Deletion API (DeleteProjectData) and a Console action that initiates a deletion job.
- Primary data removal (live indexes and object stores) is completed within 48 hours of a deletion request.
- Snapshot/backups: our backup retention window is up to 90 days for offsite backups; backups are scheduled for purge on the next maintenance cycle and are fully purged within that window.
- Final confirmation: we provide a deletion certificate once the job completes.

Q: Self-serve vs manual
- Enterprise (EU tenancy) customers get the DeleteProjectData endpoint and can trigger immediate deletion. For customers on shared/off-the-shelf plans, we handle deletion requests via support and confirm completion within the same timelines.

Q: Compliance artifacts / DPA
- Attached: redwood-soc2-summary-2025.pdf and a concise data-retention-matrix (data-retention-matrix-202605.pdf).
- We also provided a standard DPA — if you want changes we can process them via DocuSign.

Notes / operational considerations:
- Deletion removes data from active storage and indexes. Derived artifacts used for model-quality research (anonymized aggregates) are not tied to customer identifiers and are excluded from project-level deletions. If you prefer complete exclusion, we can include a contract clause to block use for research.
- EU tenancy includes region-bound keys (KMS integration) and restricted SRE access via our zero-trust controls.

Next steps: If this looks OK, confirm EU tenancy and I’ll open a DPA DocuSign with the Europa Consult legal team.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Sales — EMEA
Redwood Inference

Hi Lena — quick answers to your follow-ups and I pasted formal wording you can use in the procurement packet. Also attached the DPA draft and a DocuSign envelope link.

1) SLA / contractual wording (suggested clause for procurement):
"Redwood Inference shall, upon Customer's written request or via Customer-initiated deletion through the Redwood Admin API, remove Customer Data from primary storage within forty-eight (48) hours. Redwood shall use commercially reasonable efforts to purge Customer Data from backups and nearline snapshots within ninety (90) days. Redwood will provide Customer with written confirmation/certificate of deletion upon completion of the deletion process."

2) Is 48 hours SLA-backed?
- For Enterprise EU tenancies and contracts that include the Data Protection Addendum, the 48-hour primary deletion window can be included as a contractual SLA (remedy and reporting obligations available). For self-serve accounts the 48-hour figure is an operational target and deletion is handled via support.

3) Backup encryption / key handling
- Backups are encrypted at rest using customer-specific KMS keys for EU-tenancies. Key material is managed via our KMS integration; key rotation and key deletion follow the DPA terms. When a customer requests deletion and also requests KMS key destruction as part of the flow, we will coordinate key destruction subject to legal hold limitations and provide a confirmation. Note: in most cloud architectures a destroyed key will render encrypted backups unrecoverable; we only perform key destruction upon explicit contract/legal request.

Documents / links attached: Europa_DPA_v1.3.docx (DPA draft), redwood-soc2-summary-2025.pdf, data-retention-matrix-202605.pdf. DocuSign: https://docusign.example.com/ENVELOPE-56789
